text: Server hardening: revoke sessions on password change, request size cap, security headers

Done in e7c6fd6. All four items landed; 146 server tests green.

1. Session revoke on password change: change_password gained a required
   current_token param; deletes all auth_tokens for the account except that
   token's hash. Route passes g.token. change_email deliberately left unchanged
   (the ticket marked it optional; an email change isn't a compromise response).
2. Request cap: DEFAULT_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH = 4 MB applied in create_blueprint's
   record_once. Gotcha handled: Flask pre-seeds MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH=None, so
   setdefault() is a no-op — used `if get(...) is None` instead so an operator's
   explicit value still wins. Oversized -> 413 payload_too_large via a JSON error
   handler matching the ApiError envelope shape.
3. Security headers: single app-wide after_request, registered once (guarded via
   app.extensions flag so multi-mount doesn't stack duplicates). Baseline
   (nosniff + Referrer-Policy: no-referrer) on every response; CSP +
   X-Frame-Options: DENY on text/html only. CSP = default-src 'self' (script-src
   inherits strict 'self' — no inline scripts on either HTML page), style-src
   adds 'unsafe-inline' (invite.html inline <style> + SPA runtime styles),
   img-src 'self' data:, object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', frame-ancestors
   'none'. All headers use setdefault so a proxy's own headers aren't clobbered.
4. README: Configuration row for MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH override; Deployment
   requirements now lists what the blueprint handles itself (cap, headers,
   revocation) and the accepted account-enumeration trade-off.

Verification note: server pytest isn't installed by default here — I created
server/.venv (gitignored) via `pip install -e ".[dev]"` to run it. CSP was
crafted against the actual committed web_dist/index.html (external /assets/ JS+CSS,
no inline script) and templates/invite.html (inline <style>); if the web build
later introduces an inline <script>, script-src would need a nonce/hash.
